html:
SMTO-FIL-0047 — SMTO stopped a save to a different place than the drive you chose

GUID: 215c0ee8-3832-4ab9-ad1f-6d45ed9a5e7d
Slug: destination-mismatch
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • SMTO was about to save files somewhere other than the drive or folder you picked, so it stopped before writing anything. Nothing was copied or changed by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, tell SMTO to save the files inside the drive or folder you chose earlier, and type its full folder path. SMTO only allows saving inside the place you picked, so the next attempt has to point there.
  2. If you really meant a different place, say so plainly and give its full folder path, for example "copy the files to /media/backup". SMTO never switches to another drive on its own; a new place has to come from you.
  3. Before it copies again, ask SMTO to list what is already in the destination folder. Files from earlier steps may already be there, so you can avoid copying them twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the copy and the files appear in the drive or folder you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Removable destination protection in Settings just to get past this; it is what kept the files from going to the wrong drive.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The removable-destination guard vetoed a write because its destination operand lies outside the bound mount point or explicitly named path for this Gateway scope; nothing was dispatched.

What this means

  • The proposed destination lies outside the explicitly selected path/volume, or arguments identify another removable mount instead of the bound one. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The proposed destination lies outside the explicitly selected path/volume, or arguments identify another removable mount instead of the bound one.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the current selected volume/path binding with the actual copy/move destination and revalidate its identity.

How to fix it

  • Compare the proposed destination in the tool arguments with the binding stored under removable_destination_resolution in the run state (the error carries the bound destination). Have the model target a path inside the bound mount, or have the user name a new destination explicitly; the guard never rewrites commands. The guard is controlled by removable_destination_guard_enabled (Settings › Security › Removable destination protection).
  • Use the selected destination path and revalidate its current volume identity. If a different destination is intended, select it explicitly before writing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The proposed destination matches the user's current explicit selection.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
